01. Have you attached your transcripts for all completed units or degrees? Options: Yes | No | Not Applicable

Provide administrative leadership and operational oversight for South Merced Center facilities, services, partnerships, community activities, and the site support necessary for approved College programs.

Develop, implement, and evaluate site operational plans, facility-use procedures, service standards, performance measures, and continuous improvement initiatives aligned with District priorities and community needs.
Establish and oversee procedures and ensure compliance with District policies, collective bargaining agreements, legal requirements, grants, contracts, and partnership agreements.
Manage and coordinate daily Center operations, including scheduling, facilities use, technology resources, safety preparedness, and coordination with District support departments.

Assess community and workforce needs and collaborate with College stakeholders to identify and coordinate access, facility, scheduling, site-readiness, and operational-support needs for approved educational, workforce development, adult education, and community education offerings, including technology, registration access, marketing coordination, and student communications.
Support outreach and access activities that connect community members with educational and career pathways.
Develop and maintain partnerships with employers, workforce agencies, and regional organizations to support community access to workforce opportunities and inform site-based service needs.

Coordinate facility access, scheduling, referrals, site logistics, and community resource networks that support the delivery of enrollment, financial aid, counseling, tutoring, career services, disability support, basic needs, and related student services and address barriers to student success.
Promote equitable, culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and student-centered practices that support access, retention, and achievement.

Lead outreach, recruitment, and community engagement strategies that increase awareness, participation, and enrollment, particularly among underserved populations; coordinate facility use, logistics, scheduling, and community communications for related events, workshops, orientations, and enrollment campaigns.

Develop and maintain collaborative partnerships with educational institutions, government agencies, employers, nonprofit organizations, philanthropic entities, and community groups; serve as the primary site liaison for South Merced Center initiatives by facilitating stakeholder engagement, gathering community input, and supporting partnership development.

Coordinate site access, operational support, and community engagement for youth- and family-focused educational, enrichment, college-access, college-awareness, career-exploration, and postsecondary-planning activities in collaboration with College departments and community partners, including family-centered workshops and community learning opportunities.

Collect, analyze, and report data related to Center utilization, facility access, service utilization, community participation, workforce outcomes, and community impact; use labor market information, community needs assessments, stakeholder feedback, and performance metrics to inform planning, service coordination, facility use, resource allocation, and continuous improvement.
Prepare reports, strategic plans, grant applications, recommendations, and related documents while administering grants, contracts, budgets, and other assigned resources.
Coordinate, support, and provide operational direction to assigned staff, student workers, volunteers, consultants, and temporary employees; perform supervisory responsibilities as assigned.
Establish work priorities, schedules, performance expectations, and professional development opportunities while ensuring compliance with District procedures and safe work practices.
Represent the Center in College and District planning efforts and foster an inclusive, equitable environment that supports student success, employee engagement, and community collaboration.
Perform other duties as assigned.
The mission, organization, governance, and funding structure of California Community Colleges.
Provide leadership for assigned operations of a comprehensive community-based educational center, including facilities, access, scheduling, safety, and service coordination.
Community-based educational center operations, site administration, facilities coordination, and service delivery models.
Coordinate the cross-departmental site access, facilities, logistics, and operational support for educational, workforce, and student-support initiatives.
The operational coordination and site-based support of instructional programs, student services, and student success initiatives in a community college.
Build and sustain productive community partnerships, maintain effective working relationships with diverse constituencies, and represent the College effectively.
Adult education, noncredit education, workforce development systems, career education pathways, and labor market trends.
Analyze data, identify service-delivery gaps, and use findings to improve Center operations and resource decisions.
Enrollment management, outreach, recruitment, retention, and student success practices.
Develop and implement procedures, manage site operations, and resolve complex operational issues.
Community engagement, partnership development, interagency collaboration, and public communication strategies.
Manage multiple priorities, budgets, grants, projects, and deadlines while meeting institutional objectives.
Student Equity and Achievement, Guided Pathways, Basic Needs, accessibility, and equity-minded service practices.
Supervise, motivate, develop, and evaluate assigned staff.
Site operations planning, service coordination, utilization assessment, data analysis, and continuous improvement.
Demonstrate cultural humility, equity-minded leadership, and community-centered engagement practices.
Budget development and control, grant and contract administration, and fiscal management.
Interpret and apply laws, regulations, policies, collective bargaining agreements, contracts, and approved partnership agreements.
Applicable state and federal laws, District policies, and compliance requirements, including Title 5 and FERPA.
Principles of supervision, collective bargaining agreements, performance management, and employee development.
Communicate effectively orally and in writing, including preparing reports, proposals, and presentations.
